scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: URGENT!! The Internet Lab has DISAPPEARED for the
whole Office department!! All morning none of the 128.168.0.x machines answer
any of our PCs (we're the 192.168.3.x ones) -- everything else works, it's
just the lab that's gone. The link that carries us over to the lab is
obviously DOWN -- the wire between the routers on that side has died and
nobody has noticed!! Please bring the link to the Internet Lab back up -- we
need their machines TODAY!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
There is no fault in the network. The helpdesk ticket's claim that the wan_r1_r2
link has "died" and that the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) is unreachable from the
Office department (192.168.3.x) does not match the actual state of the network.

Every component along the reported path was examined directly:

1. Physical layer — router1's eth3 (20.20.0.1/8) and router2's eth2 (20.20.0.2/8),
   which form the wan_r1_r2 segment, are both in state UP/LOWER_UP with no errors.
   The wan_r0_r1 segment (10.0.0.0/8) is equally healthy.

2. Routing layer — RIP has fully converged on all three routers. Router1 carries
   the route 128.168.0.0/16 via 20.20.0.2 (router2) at metric 2 in its FIB, and
   router2 carries 192.168.3.0/24 via 20.20.0.1 (router1) at metric 2. Router0
   also holds the full topology.

3. End-to-end reachability — live pings from office_pc (192.168.3.2) to pc2
   (128.168.0.2) and pc3 (128.168.0.3) returned 0% packet loss at ~1.6 ms RTT.
   Internet Lab hosts have correct IP addresses and a correct default gateway
   (128.168.0.1 = router2).

Root cause: There is no fault. The reported symptom is a false premise; the
network has been functioning correctly throughout.

Corrective action: No configuration or hardware change is required. Advise the
reporting user to re-test connectivity from their workstation, as the issue may
have been transient or originate from the client machine itself rather than the
network infrastructure.
